risk_if_not_implemented: Without AI & Autonomous Technologies Registration, AI and autonomous systems may produce unreliable, biased or unsafe outputs, act outside authorized scope, or expose sensitive data. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Regulatory / Legal / Contractual Financial Liability (R-EX-5), Loss of Authorization / Certification / License (R-EX-11), Sensitive Data / Compliance Exposure from Unsanctioned AI Use (R-AI-4), and most likely increases susceptibility to Human Error (MT-9), Statutory / Regulatory / Contractual Change (MT-11).

compensating_control_1.name: Sensitive / Regulated Data Governance
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate data governance so that sensitive and/or regulated data is effectively managed and maintained in accordance with applicable statutory, regulatory and contractual obligations.
compensating_control_1.justification: Sensitive / Regulated Data Governance (DCH-03) provides policy-level governance that compensates for the absence of AI & Autonomous Technologies Registration (CPL-28) by establishing documented expectations, accountability structures, and organizational guardrails. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance
compensating_control_2.description: Mechanisms exist to facilitate the identification and implementation of relevant statutory, regulatory and contractual controls.
compensating_control_2.justification: Statutory, Regulatory & Contractual Compliance (CPL-02) provides overlapping security capability that compensates for the absence of AI & Autonomous Technologies Registration (CPL-28) by addressing related risk objectives through an alternative control mechanism aligned with Process applicability. Given the process-oriented nature of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
